+@@ -369,6 +370,49 @@ class IntegrationTestsBase(unittest.TestCase):

++
++    def try_and_settle(self, try_func, wait_interfaces_try=None, wait_interfaces_after=None):
++        '''Run `netplan try`, wait for the configuration to apply, run `try_func` and allow try to time out'''
++
++        # Because `netplan try` uses select(2) to implement the timeout, stdin
++        # needs to be a stream that is never ready to read.
++        # Use mkstemp to avoid prior failures' leftovers.
++        (fifo_tmp, fifo_path) = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="netplan-try-test")
++        os.close(fifo_tmp)
++        os.unlink(fifo_path)
++
++        os.mkfifo(fifo_path)
++        fifo = os.open(fifo_path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NONBLOCK)
++
++        try:
++            timeout = 10
++
++            proc = subprocess.Popen(["netplan", "try", f"--timeout={timeout}"], stdin=fifo)
++
++            # wait for apply to finish
++            wait_duration = 0
++            while not pathlib.Path("/run/netplan/netplan-try.ready").exists():
++                wait_duration += 0.1
++                time.sleep(0.1)
++
++                if wait_duration > timeout:
++                    break
++
++            self.settle(wait_interfaces=wait_interfaces_try)
++
++            try_func()
++
++            proc.wait()
++            self.settle(wait_interfaces=wait_interfaces_after)
++        finally:
++            # don't step on other tests
++            proc.wait()
++            os.close(fifo)
++            os.unlink(fifo_path)
++
++    def settle(self, wait_interfaces=None, state_dir=None):
+         # start NM so that we can verify that it does not manage anything
+         subprocess.call(['nm-online', '-sxq'])  # Wait for NM startup, from 'netplan apply'
+         if not self.is_active('NetworkManager.service'):

++
++        with open(self.config, 'w') as f:
++            f.write('''network:
++  renderer: %(r)s
++  ethernets:
++    %(e2c)s:
++      dhcp4: false
++      addresses: [192.168.6.201/24]''' % {'r': self.backend, 'e2c': self.dev_e2_client})
++
++        def assert_static_ip():
++            self.assert_iface_up(self.dev_e2_client,
++                                 ['inet 192.168.6.201/24'])
++
++        self.try_and_settle(assert_static_ip,
++                            wait_interfaces_try=[
++                                self.state(self.dev_e2_client, "inet 192.168.6.201"),
++                            ],
++                            wait_interfaces_after=[
++                                # Use "dynamic" instead of state_dhcp4 since
++                                # state_dhcp4 will match our static address.
++                                self.state(self.dev_e2_client, "dynamic"),
++                            ])
++
++        self.assert_file_permissions()
++        self.assert_iface_up(self.dev_e2_client,
++                             expected_ip_a=['inet 192.168.6.[0-9]+/24'],
++                             unexpected_ip_a=['inet 192.168.6.201/24'])

diff --git a/debian/patches/lp2083029/0007-cli-ConfigManager-must-copy-file-ownership.patch b/debian/patches/lp2083029/0007-cli-ConfigManager-must-copy-file-ownership.patch

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+From: Wesley Hershberger <wesley.hershberger@canonical.com>
+Date: Mon, 24 Mar 2025 13:30:57 -0500
+Subject: cli: ConfigManager must copy file ownership
+
+systemd-networkd will not read .netdev and .network files unless the
+group is set to 'systemd-network'.
+
+Origin: https://github.com/canonical/netplan/commit/a1a169f996a576ff3ca5f2583c529f6cd231e9ab
+Bug: https://bugs.launchpad.net/netplan/+bug/2083029
+---
+ netplan_cli/configmanager.py | 8 +++++++-
+ 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
+
+diff --git a/netplan_cli/configmanager.py b/netplan_cli/configmanager.py
+index 59e8b88..54cee80 100644
+--- a/netplan_cli/configmanager.py
++++ b/netplan_cli/configmanager.py
+@@ -153,7 +153,7 @@ class ConfigManager(object):
+ 
+     def _copy_tree(self, src, dst, missing_ok=False):
+         try:
+-            shutil.copytree(src, dst)
++            shutil.copytree(src, dst, copy_function=copy_with_ownership)
+         except FileNotFoundError:
+             if missing_ok:
+                 pass
+@@ -161,6 +161,12 @@ class ConfigManager(object):
+                 raise
+ 
+ 
++def copy_with_ownership(src, dst, follow_symlinks=True):
++    shutil.copy2(src, dst, follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks)
++    stat = os.stat(src, follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks)
++    os.chown(dst, stat.st_uid, stat.st_gid, follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks)
++
++

+     """
+     Configuration could not be parsed or has otherwise failed to apply
diff --git a/debian/patches/lp2083029/0008-generate-Don-t-run-during-netplan-try.patch b/debian/patches/lp2083029/0008-generate-Don-t-run-during-netplan-try.patch

index 0000000..e3c7b9b
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+From: Wesley Hershberger <wesley.hershberger@canonical.com>
+Date: Tue, 25 Mar 2025 09:11:56 -0500
+Subject: generate: Don't run during `netplan try`
+
+Generate may be called by NetworkManager (via Dbus) in Ubuntu >23.10.
+
+While `netplan try` is waiting for revert, there is no situation where
+the generator should be called.
+
+Origin: https://github.com/canonical/netplan/commit/f9e35f66938695581098e91030be1ec71c36b865
+Bug: https://bugs.launchpad.net/netplan/+bug/2083029
+---
+ src/generate.c               | 17 +++++++++++++++++
+ tests/generator/base.py      |  1 +
+ tests/generator/test_args.py |  6 ++++++
+ 3 files changed, 24 insertions(+)
+
+diff --git a/src/generate.c b/src/generate.c
+index aa52324..52405f0 100644
+--- a/src/generate.c
++++ b/src/generate.c
+@@ -208,6 +208,7 @@ int main(int argc, char** argv)
+     /* are we being called as systemd generator? */
+     gboolean called_as_generator = (strstr(argv[0], "systemd/system-generators/") != NULL);
+     g_autofree char* generator_run_stamp = NULL;
++    g_autofree char* netplan_try_stamp = NULL;
+     glob_t gl;
+     int error_code = 0;
+     char* ignore_errors_env = NULL;
+@@ -243,6 +244,22 @@ int main(int argc, char** argv)
+         }
+     }
+ 
++    // The file at netplan_try_stamp is created while `netplan try` is waiting
++    // for user confirmation. If generate is triggered while netplan try is
++    // running, we shouldn't regenerate the configuration.
++    // We can be called by either systemd (as a generator during daemon-reload)
++    // or by NetworkManager when it is reloading configuration (Ubuntu >23.10),
++    // see https://netplan.readthedocs.io/en/stable/netplan-everywhere/.
++    // LP #2083029
++    netplan_try_stamp = g_build_path(G_DIR_SEPARATOR_S,
++                                     rootdir != NULL ? rootdir : G_DIR_SEPARATOR_S,
++                                     "run", "netplan", "netplan-try.ready",
++                                     NULL);
++    if (g_access(netplan_try_stamp, F_OK) == 0) {
++        g_fprintf(stderr, "'netplan try' is restoring configuration, remove %s to force re-run.\n", netplan_try_stamp);
++        return 1;
++    }
++
+     if ((ignore_errors_env = getenv("NETPLAN_PARSER_IGNORE_ERRORS"))) {
+         // This is used mostly by autopkgtests
+         // LCOV_EXCL_START
